content: Standard secrets-manager audit logging captures: what secret was accessed/created/updated/deleted, when, by what actor/process, whether the action succeeded or was denied, and any anomalous access patterns (e.g. repeated failed unlock attempts). Audit logs must be resilient to tampering/deletion by the same process that can access secrets (append-only log, ideally hash-chained or stored separately from the vault data) so a compromise of the vault doesn't silently erase its own trail. For a single-user local app, an append-only SQLite table (or a separate log file) recording entry_id, action, timestamp, and outcome is sufficient; full tamper-evidence (hash chaining) is a nice-to-have, not a hard requirement, given there's no adversarial multi-tenant threat model.
